# ShiftMate synthetic dataset schema

**Status:** schema decision for the generator (technical spec §8.22, task T35); no data is generated by this document.  
**Schema version:** `1.2.0` · **Owner:** ShiftMate product/engineering · **Date:** 24 September 2026

## 1. Decision and boundaries

The generated dataset is a **relational bundle plus an append-only event stream**, not one wide CSV. A wide row cannot faithfully express a task with several waits, a corrected explanation, repeated alert transitions, missing signals, and two operators across shifts. The bundle supports task-time estimation, comparable usage history, the demo's first-launch history, and the IsolationForest comparison. It does **not** represent real Cat telemetry or measured field performance.

`docs/PRODUCT_PLAN.md` controls behaviour; `docs/TECHNICAL_SPEC.md` controls runtime contracts (enums §5.1, ledger payloads §5.3, profiles §5.4.1, generator §8.22). This schema fixes the structure and meaning of the generated files and must stay consistent with both. Every ledger kind/subtype, enum spelling and ID format used here is the technical spec's.

**Three kinds of information must remain distinct:**

1. **Pre-start inputs**: assignment, profile, operator experience at that date, and the condition forecast available when the estimate was made. Only these are estimator features.
2. **Observed/reported events**: time-stamped signals, reports, task actions, detections, and alert transitions. Reports are claims until corroborated or reviewed; the latest correction changes the effective view without erasing history.
3. **Outcomes**: actual task duration/output, final idle class and incident outcome. They are available for training/evaluation **after** the event, never to the live estimator or rules under test.

**Notation:** `!` required, `?` nullable; `id` is a string key; `ts` is ISO 8601 UTC with millisecond precision (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ`); `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD` in site-local time; `int`, `float`, `bool`, and `str` have their usual JSON meanings. CSV numbers use a dot decimal and no thousands separators; booleans are `true`/`false`; nullable CSV fields are empty, never `0`, `unknown`, or `NA`. JSONL uses `null`. All numeric quantities are finite. Every file is UTF-8 with LF and a header for CSV.

Generated bundle (`data/generated/`, and `data/generated/sens_<scale>/` for sensitivity runs):

| File | One row/object per | Primary key | Used by (technical spec) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `manifest.json` | bundle | — | reproducibility checks (TC-62), eval banner (§12.6) |
| `sites.csv` | site | `site_id` | FK target; job efficiency, congestion, darkness, diesel price, local time (§8.4, §8.6, §8.7) |
| `zones.csv` | site zone | `zone_id` | FK target; speed limits, near-miss/overspeed zone grouping (§8.5, §8.21) |
| `operators.csv` | fictional operator | `operator_id` | estimator features at task date, split B (§8.22) |
| `machines.csv` | detailed machine | `machine_id` | profile/version, machine age (§8.6.2) |
| `fleet.csv` | machine status snapshot | `machine_id` | fleet view seed for 100 machines (S6, T44) |
| `shifts.csv` | operator-machine shift | `shift_id` | FK target; "last 5 shifts" comparisons (§8.8) |
| `tasks.csv` | assigned task and final outcome | `task_id` | estimator training and evaluation (§8.22), expected waiting (§8.6.5), impact preview inputs (§8.6.9) |
| `conditions_hourly.csv` | site forecast valid hour | `condition_id` | pre-start weather/visibility/temperature features (§8.6.2) |
| `summaries_5m.csv` | machine five-minute window | `summary_id` | usage history, fuel per cycle (§8.8), IsolationForest (T45) |
| `idle_events.csv` | complete or open idle interval | `idle_event_id` | idle classes and attribution (§8.7, §8.8) |
| `alerts.csv` | one alert lifecycle transition | `alert_event_id` | belt/overspeed/proximity repeat patterns (§8.8) |
| `ledger_entries.jsonl` | one append-only ledger entry | `entry_id` | canonical history; source of every flat file and of `demo_history.json` (§5.3, §8.22) |

**Separate authored artifacts (not generated, not in `data/generated/`):**

| Artifact | Owner | Schema |
|---|---|---|
| `data/scenarios/*.yaml` | team (challenge scenarios by a non-rule author, E-07) | technical spec §5.4.6. Source of every 1 Hz signal stream, proximity episode, sensor dropout and scripted expectation (`expect`), plus `author_role` |
| `data/voice_test/utterances.jsonl` | team, human reviewed | §4.6 below |
| `data/voice_train/intent_examples.jsonl` | coding model drafts, human reviewed (E-06) | §4.6 below |
| `packages/content/seed/demo_seed.json` | team, hand-authored | technical spec §5.4.2; sites, zones, machines, operators, console users, pairing codes |
| `packages/content/seed/demo_history.json` | generated projection | last 14 days of `ledger_entries.jsonl` for EX-07, HT-03 and their operators, with day offsets (technical spec §5.4.2). The generator pins OP-0007 to 1 completed trenching task and no task started in rain, dust or darkness, so the demo's rain forecast triggers condition prep |
| `data/organiser/raw/` | organiser, verbatim | never modified; mapped by `data/organiser/mapping.yaml` |

**Deliberately not in the bundle** (the technical spec produces this information elsewhere, so a generated file would be a second, unused copy): impact previews (a derived view; the `ImpactSummary` is carried by `report/reassignment_request` and `report/supervisor_notification` entries); Safe Exit advisories (they are `A-EXIT-UNSEC` alert transitions in `alerts.csv`/ledger); alert-budget counters and per-decision interaction logs (engine snapshot telemetry read by the eval harness, §8.3); incident projections (ledger incident family entries); incident replay comparisons (S9 replay is isolated and never persisted); proximity detections and 1 Hz signal samples (scenario YAML is the source; incident snapshots carry the captured window); scenario oracle labels (the YAML `expect` blocks); intent decisions (diagnostics/eval output, §8.13.4).

The reference files do not duplicate secrets. Demo PIN hashes, console accounts, and pairing codes belong in `demo_seed.json`, not in the analytical dataset. `fleet.csv` contains a status snapshot for all 100 machines; `machines.csv` contains details for its 24 detailed machines. The remaining 76 fleet rows are status-only.

Flat operational files are **projections**, not a second mutable truth: `summary_id` equals its `observation/signal_summary_5m` ledger `entry_id`; `alert_event_id` equals the corresponding `alert/*` ledger `entry_id`; `idle_event_id` is the logical interval ID referenced by its `idle_event/*`, `report/idle_reason` and `inference/idle_classification` entries; `shift_id` is the ID used by its `shift_event/start` entry.

## 3. Cross-cutting rules

### 3.1 Provenance and time

Every generated row has `data_origin! = synthetic:gen-1.0:<seed>`; rows copied from the demo seed use `demo_seed` (technical spec D-11). Every operational record has `observed_at!` (when it happened) and `recorded_at!` (when it was saved), or the table's more precise `started_at`/`window_start` equivalent. Server receipt time is not generated; the importer/sync test adds it on delivery and it never overwrites event time. Reference records use `created_at!`. Conditions use `issued_at!` and validity bounds because a forecast issued after a task's estimate was requested cannot be used as a pre-start feature. Rows within each file sort ascending by the grain's time, then by ID.

The generator never silently fills missing signals. Sensor absence is represented by a null metric plus `missing_signal_names`; stale is calculated from the last real timestamp and the machine profile's freshness limit. A zero speed, zero fuel, false belt state, and absent reading have different meanings.

IDs follow technical spec §5.1: UUID v4 syntax for shifts, ledger entries, idle events, alerts and incidents (generated deterministically from the seeded RNG); readable IDs for sites (`SITE-CHN-01`), zones (`Z-CHN-TR1`), operators (`OP-0007`), machines (`EX-07`) and tasks (`T-<YYYYMMDD>-<MACHINE>-<n>`). Foreign keys must resolve within this bundle or the demo seed. Each generated ledger entry's `device_id` is one fixed synthetic device UUID per machine.

### 3.2 Privacy and leakage

Use fictional names. No birth dates, demographic attributes, exact personal location tracks, real voice recordings, PINs, passwords, or raw free text about a real person are generated. `operator_id` is an operational key, **not an estimator feature**. `language` supports UI/voice testing, **not speed prediction**. Individual hidden operator effects may be used by the generator; they are documented in `docs/GENERATOR_ASSUMPTIONS.md` and are not exported as model inputs. Entries with `audience = operator_only` (`learning_event/*`, `report/recommendation_feedback`, `inference/recommendation`, own findings) may appear in `ledger_entries.jsonl` and `demo_history.json` (device history) but never in anything imported to the server (technical spec §6.2 push rules).

`tasks.csv` has a documented **feature cutoff** at `estimate_requested_at`. Columns under "outcome" cannot appear in training X, even if the CSV stores them beside features. Likewise `idle_events`' final class and reason, alert transitions and incident outcomes cannot be joined to pre-start predictions. Split A is weeks 1–8 train, 9–10 calibration, 11–12 test; split B holds out eight fixed operators (technical spec §8.22). The `split_*` columns are metadata, never features. Comparable-history features must be computed only from events before the prediction time.

## 4. Exact column dictionary

### 4.1 Reference and schedule

**`sites.csv`** — one site (mirrors server `sites`, technical spec §5.2). Values come from the demo seed (`data_origin=demo_seed`).

| Column | Type | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `site_id!` | id | Foreign key for conditions, tasks, zones and fair same-site comparisons. |
| `name!` | str | Human-readable briefing and console label. |
| `sector!` | enum `construction/mining` | Keeps excavator and haul contexts separate. |
| `lat!`, `lon!` | float | Approximate fictional site placement; no operator track. |
| `utc_offset_minutes!` | int | Converts UTC events to site-local shift date and time of day. |
| `diesel_price_inr_per_l!` | float | Engine-off cost estimate (F9-R3). |
| `dark_start_local!`, `dark_end_local!` | `HH:MM` | Darkness modifier and night theme. |
| `job_efficiency_override?` | float `(0,1]` | Per-site job efficiency (product F4); null uses the profile's `job_efficiency`. |
| `congestion_level!` | `low/medium/high` | Current site congestion used at runtime (§8.6.2); history uses `tasks.site_congestion_at_start`. |
| `data_origin!`, `created_at!` | str, ts | Auditable source and chronology. |

**`zones.csv`** — one zone, not a GPS trace (mirrors server `zones`).

| Column | Type | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `zone_id!`, `site_id!` | id, id | Zone identity and site guard. |
| `name!`, `kind!` | str, enum `trench_area/loading_bay/yard/haul_road/shovel/crusher/dump/other` | Briefing location and comparable incident grouping. |
| `center_lat!`, `center_lon!`, `radius_m!` | float, float, float `>0` | Fictional geofence context; not a safety-certified boundary. |
| `speed_limit_kmh?` | float `>0` | Overspeed rule; null uses the profile default. |
| `data_origin!`, `created_at!` | str, ts | Provenance. |

**`operators.csv`** — 48 fictional operators (mirrors server `operators` without PIN fields). Experience is also snapshotted on each task so a later value is never used for an earlier job.

| Column | Type | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `operator_id!`, `site_id!` | id, id | Shift assignment and site-scoped history. |
| `display_name!` | str | Fictional demo display only. |
| `language!` | `en/hi/ta` | Voice/content routing; excluded from estimator X. |
| `skill_level!` | `beginner/intermediate/expert` | Guidance defaults and estimator feature. |
| `experience_months!` | int `>=0` | Experience at the generator anchor date; tasks carry their own dated value. |
| `hired_at!` | date | First-30-day Guided mode and dated experience. |
| `regular_machine_class!` | `excavator/haul_truck/wheel_loader` | Plausible assignments and split-B balance (4 excavator + 4 truck operators held out). |
| `data_origin!`, `created_at!` | str, ts | Provenance. |

**`machines.csv`** — 24 detailed machines: 10 excavators, 6 wheel loaders, 8 haul trucks. Profile JSON remains the authoritative source for rates, freshness and rule thresholds. Wheel loaders are a profile-only class (product F16, technical spec F16-R4): they have detailed rows but **no generated tasks, idle events or summaries**.

| Column | Type | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `machine_id!`, `short_id!`, `site_id!` | id, int `1..65535`, id | Operational key, SOS packet key, site assignment. |
| `profile_id!`, `profile_version!` | id, int | Reproducible baseline/rules; prevents silent profile drift. |
| `machine_class!`, `model_name!` | enum `excavator/haul_truck/wheel_loader`, str | Stratification and visible machine label. |
| `year_of_manufacture!` | int | Machine age at task start; no current-age leakage. |
| `detail_level!` | literal `detailed` | Eligible for task/signal history. |
| `data_origin!`, `created_at!` | str, ts | Provenance. |

**`fleet.csv`** — status snapshot for all 100 machines (mirrors server `fleet_status`). Twenty-four rows link to `machines.csv`; the other 76 have no detailed history.

| Column | Type | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `machine_id!`, `short_id!`, `site_id!` | id, int, id | Identity and join to details when available. |
| `machine_class!`, `profile_id!`, `profile_version!` | enum, id, int | Profile-compatible display and filters. |

| Column | Type | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|

| `started_at!`, `ended_at?` | ts | Shift window for alert counts, idle repeats and handover. |
| `local_shift_date!` | date | Prevents UTC midnight from splitting a night shift. |
| `shift_code!` | `day/evening/night` | Shift start 06:00 / 14:00 / 22:00 site-local (technical spec §8.22). |

### 4.2 Estimator table: `tasks.csv`

One row is an assignment (server `task_assignments` / `TaskAssignment` wire shape) plus its final outcome (`task_event/complete` payload). **A completed row is training eligible only when `actual_active_min>0`, required pre-start inputs are available, and task type/profile/unit are supported by the machine class's estimator.** Cancelled or open rows still matter to the task board and are not dropped.

| Column | Type | Why it exists / availability |
|---|---|---|
| `task_id!`, `assignment_revision!` | id, int `>=1` | Stable assignment key and revision; revision is not an ML feature. |
| `site_id!`, `zone_id?`, `machine_id!`, `operator_id!`, `shift_id?` | ids | Assignment and comparable context; shift may be unknown before sign-in. |
| `task_type!`, `material!`, `quantity!`, `unit!` | str, str, float `>0`, Unit | Baseline rate and model features; unit must match the profile task type. |
| `location_text!`, `priority!`, `completion_criterion!` | str, int `1..3`, str | Task board and explicit definition of done; not estimator features. |
| `assignment_source!` | `dispatcher/seed/reassignment` | Who assigned the work (server `source`). |
| `planned_date!`, `sequence!` | date, int `>=1` | Board order; the impact preview selects the next task by this immutable sequence (§8.6.9). |
| `planned_start_at?`, `planned_start_window_min!` | ts, int `0..240` | Planned start window `[planned_start_at, planned_start_at + planned_start_window_min)` (technical spec §6.2, §8.6.9; default 15). A null `planned_start_at` (≈ 10 % of rows) means no window, so downstream impact is "unavailable" (product F4-R11). |
| `estimate_requested_at!` | ts | Feature cutoff; the forecast join uses it. |
| `planner_minutes?` | float `>0` | Planner comparison (F4-R7); never an estimator feature or target. |
| `profile_id!`, `profile_version!` | id, int | Freeze the baseline constants used on that task. |
| `skill_level_at_start!`, `experience_months_at_start!`, `machine_age_years_at_start!` | enum, int, int | Features as known then; machine age = year of planned start − year of manufacture. |
| `condition_id?`, `weather_at_start?`, `visibility_at_start?`, `temperature_band_at_start?` | id, `clear/rain/windy/dusty/foggy`, `good/moderate/poor`, `cool/mild/hot/extreme` | Pre-start context from the forecast hour covering the planned start (`planned_start_at ?? estimate_requested_at`), derived exactly as technical spec §8.6.2. Forecast must have `issued_at <= estimate_requested_at`; null when none was available (runtime fallback is separate from stored raw context). |
| `time_of_day_at_start!`, `site_congestion_at_start!`, `darkness_at_start!` | `morning/afternoon/evening/night`, `low/medium/high`, bool | Time-of-day band of the planned start; the day's sampled site congestion; whether the planned start falls in the site's dark window. Together with `weather_at_start` these equal the `context` of the task's original `inference/estimate` entry, which the device uses to count condition exposure for condition prep (product F10-R12). |
| `baseline_minutes?` | float `>0` | §8.6.1 from the frozen profile, quantity, material and `sites.job_efficiency_override ?? profile.job_efficiency`; null when unsupported. |
| `status!` | TaskState | Board lifecycle; outcome fields stay null until completed. |
| **Outcome** `actual_start_at?`, `actual_end_at?` | ts | Outcome chronology, not pre-start features. |
| **Outcome** `actual_active_min?`, `actual_waiting_min?`, `actual_break_min?`, `actual_paused_min?`, `actual_elapsed_min?` | float `>=0` | `task_event/complete` accounting (§8.6.7); `actual_active_min` is the training target. |
| **Outcome** `output_qty?` | float `>=0` | Completion confirmation and realised production. |
| **Outcome** `completion_quality!` | `confirmed/partial/unverified/not_applicable` | Prevents treating an unverified completion as clean training truth. |
| `training_eligible!`, `training_exclusion_reason?` | bool, str | Reproducible inclusion policy; reason required when false. |
| `split_temporal!`, `split_unseen_operator!` | `train/calibration/test/excluded` | Fixed evaluation splits; metadata only. |
| `data_origin!`, `recorded_at!` | str, ts | Synthetic disclosure and late outcome receipt. |

For completed rows, `actual_active_min + actual_waiting_min + actual_break_min + actual_paused_min = actual_elapsed_min = (actual_end_at − actual_start_at)` in minutes, ± 0.1. The Ridge target is `ln(actual_active_min / baseline_minutes)`, not wall-clock elapsed. `output_qty` may be below `quantity` for a partial completion; such a row is not training eligible. Baseline and planner values stay as they were at start; live estimate changes are ledger entries (`inference/estimate`), never overwritten into this row.

### 4.3 Conditions and machine observations

**`conditions_hourly.csv`** — one forecast per site and valid hour (mirrors server `forecasts`, primary key `(site_id, valid_from)`). The generator issues each day's forecast once, at 18:00 site-local on the previous day, so it is available to every task's pre-start estimate. This is an input record, not proof that rain occurred.

| Column | Type | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `condition_id!`, `site_id!` | id (`<site_id>:<valid_from>`), id | Stable join to a task's available forecast. |
| `valid_from!`, `valid_to!`, `issued_at!` | ts | Temporal join and leakage prevention; half-open interval `[from,to)`. |
| `weather!`, `visibility!` | `clear/rain/windy/dusty/foggy`, `good/moderate/poor` | Estimator features and risk notes. |
| `visibility_m?` | float `>=0` | Visibility banding (§8.6.2) and fog; null when only the category exists. |
| `temp_c!`, `heat_index_c?`, `wind_kmh!`, `precipitation_mm!` | floats | Heat/wind/rain rules with explicit units. |
| `source!` | `seed/open_meteo` | Runtime forecast contract; generated forecasts use `seed`. A live operator condition report is a separate `report/condition_report` entry, never backdated into the forecast. |
| `data_origin!`, `recorded_at!` | str, ts | Origin and availability. |

**`summaries_5m.csv`** — one `observation/signal_summary_5m` payload (technical spec §5.3.2), derived only from readings actually present in a half-open five-minute window, plus join context.

| Column | Type | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `summary_id!`, `site_id!`, `machine_id!`, `shift_id?`, `task_id?` | ids | Window identity and context; `task_id` groups fuel per cycle per task (§8.8). |
| `window_start!`, `window_end!`, `recorded_at!` | ts | Exact interval and receipt. |
| `engine_on_s!`, `secured_s!`, `ready_s!`, `working_s!`, `travelling_s!`, `unknown_s!`, `idle_s!` | ints `0..300` | Utilisation and conservative unknown state; state seconds sum to at most the window length. |
| `fuel_used_l?`, `load_cycles?`, `max_speed_kmh?`, `avg_load_factor_pct?`, `belt_unfastened_moving_s?` | floats/ints | Fuel per cycle, overspeed and belt history; null if the signal was unavailable. |
| `samples!`, `missing_samples!` | ints `0..300` | Coverage; `samples+missing_samples=300` for a full window. |
| `missing_signal_names!` | JSON string array | Names what was absent, not just how many timestamps are absent. |
| `profile_id!`, `profile_version!`, `data_origin!` | id, int, str | Rule/rate interpretation and origin. |

No cumulative fuel or engine-hour reading is interpolated. `fuel_used_l` is interval consumption only if both endpoints exist and pass monotonicity/quality checks; otherwise null. A five-minute summary cannot support a two-second safety decision and is never fed into the seatbelt, Safe Exit or proximity rules.

### 4.4 Idle and alert projections

**`idle_events.csv`** — one idle interval, derived from signal/task events and linked to its report entry when there is one. The class is an inference and may change after correction; this CSV is the **effective view at export**, while the ledger keeps the original and corrections.

| Column | Type | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `idle_event_id!`, `site_id!`, `machine_id!`, `operator_id?`, `shift_id?`, `task_id?`, `zone_id?` | ids | Joins the wait to task, site follow-up and operator-private review. |
| `started_at!`, `ended_at?`, `recorded_at!` | ts | Interval (`candidate_started_at` → `ended_at`); null end means ongoing. |
| `duration_s?`, `required_s!`, `non_required_s?` | ints `>=0` | Separates warm-up/cool-down/regeneration from potentially explainable time (§8.7). |
| `required_basis!` | `warmup/cooldown/regen/mixed/none` | Why an idle was required; no operator blame. |
| `idle_class!` | `required/reported/unexplained` | Rule result (`inference/idle_classification`); `reported` must point to a reason entry. |
| `reason_code?`, `reason_entry_id?`, `reason_recorded_at?` | IdleReason, id, ts | Effective operator claim and when it arrived; null for required/unexplained. |
| `category?` | `site_delay/break/other` | Time accounting and routing, derived from the reason. |
| `prompted_at?`, `prompt_answered_at?` | ts | Interruption and delayed explanation. |
| `sensor_coverage_pct!` | float `0..100` | Marks uncertain classification if required signals were missing. |
| `evidence_status!` | `reported/corroborated/unresolved/insufficient_evidence` | Never silently factual. |
| `data_origin!` | str | Provenance. |

**`alerts.csv`** — one transition per alert, so acknowledgment cannot erase an active hazard. Each row is one `alert/*` ledger entry (technical spec §5.3.2).

| Column | Type | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `alert_event_id!`, `alert_id!`, `site_id!`, `machine_id!`, `shift_id?`, `task_id?`, `zone_id?` | ids | Transition identity, grouping, scope and context. |
| `transition!` | `raised/escalated/acknowledged/cleared/reviewed` | Full lifecycle. `reviewed` rows exist only for server-authored `alert/reviewed` entries; the gen-1.0 generator does not emit them. |
| `alert_type!`, `level!` | AlertType (incl. `A-EXIT-UNSEC`), AlertLevel (incl. `ADVISORY`) | Rule output and severity (product §12). |
| `group_key!`, `occurrences!` | str, int `>=1` | One cause can raise repeated detections without alert spam. |
| `object_id?`, `object_type?`, `place?` | ids/enums | Proximity explanation; null for other alerts. |
| `distance_m?`, `ttc_s?`, `multiplier?` | floats | Why a proximity threshold fired. |
| `clear_reason?` | str | On `cleared`; for `A-EXIT-UNSEC` one of `secured/seat_and_door_restored/not_exiting`. |
| `exit_cue?`, `safe_exit_json?` | `seat_vacant/door_open/both`, JSON object | `A-EXIT-UNSEC` only: the `SafeExitDetail` (inputs with freshness, `unavailable_signals`). Unknown inputs stay null/listed, never `true`. |
| `observed_at!`, `recorded_at!` | ts | Rule time and device save time. |
| `source!` | `observed/reported/reviewed` | Raise/escalate/clear observed, acknowledge reported, review reviewed. |
| `rule_or_model_version!`, `profile_id!`, `profile_version!` | str, id, int | Threshold auditability (NFR-15). |
| `data_origin!` | str | Provenance. |

Generated history includes belt episodes, overspeed and proximity episodes (technical spec §8.22). WARNING/CRITICAL proximity raises and belt-move > 30 s have matching incident family entries in the ledger.

### 4.5 Canonical event stream

**`ledger_entries.jsonl`** follows technical spec §5.3.1 *exactly*: `entry_id!`, `device_id!`, `shift_id?`, `machine_id!`, `operator_id?`, `kind!`, `subtype!`, `source!`, `payload!`, `observed_at!`, `recorded_at!`, `freshness_s?`, `confidence?`, `rule_or_model_version?` (required for kinds `alert` and `inference`), `original_text?`, `supersedes?`, `audience!`, `data_origin!`, `sync_status!`, `chain_seq?`, `prev_hash?`, `content_hash?`, `canonical_payload?`. In this file timestamps are ISO UTC strings; the importer converts them to device epoch milliseconds. `payload` is validated by technical spec §5.3.2, not a free-form bag. Generated entries have `sync_status = confirmed`. The generated kinds are:

| Kind/subtype | Why include it in generated history |
|---|---|
| `shift_event/start,end` | Shift boundaries (`shifts.csv`). |
| `task_event/start,pause,resume,block,complete,cancel` | Task chronology and accounting (`tasks.csv`); expected waiting (§8.6.5). |
| `inference/estimate` | Original estimate per started task (F4-R5), with `context` (weather, visibility, temperature band, time of day, congestion, darkness) equal to the task's pre-start columns; condition-prep exposure is counted from it (F10-R12). |
| `observation/signal_summary_5m`, `observation/condition_forecast` | Usage history and time-aware conditions. |
| `idle_event/started,ended`; `inference/idle_classification`; `report/idle_reason`; `correction/idle_reason` | Explain-once propagation and corrected attribution. |
| `report/progress_report` | Live progress on some tasks. |
| `alert/raised,escalated,acknowledged,cleared` | Safety history independent of explanations. |
| `incident/created,snapshot_completed,status_changed`; `report/incident_report`; `inference/incident_extraction` | Incidents with 60 s pre / 30 s post snapshots; chain fields and valid hashes are required (§8.10). |
| `inference/finding`, `correction/finding` | Site/machine/needs-review routing history (§8.8). |
| `inference/recommendation`, `report/recommendation_feedback`, `learning_event/started,answered,completed,deferred` | Private learning flow (`operator_only`; device history only). Recommendation `source` includes `condition_prep` and `refresher`; `learning_event` carries `mode` (`full`/`refresher`) and, on `completed`, `refresher_opt_in` (F10-R12, F10-R13). |
| `handover_item/added,edited,acknowledged,resolved,removed`; `report/handover_note` | Acknowledged remains open until resolved. |

The `source` enum (`observed/reported/inferred/reviewed`) describes **epistemic status**; `data_origin` describes **where this record came from**. They are not interchangeable. Reports carry `original_text` only for fictional synthetic utterances. A correction points to `supersedes` and carries the replacement payload (or `null` to retract). Server-authored entries (`incident/reviewed`, `alert/reviewed`) and request entries (`report/reassignment_request`, `report/supervisor_notification`) are not generated in gen-1.0; they are created at runtime.

### 4.6 Voice (authored, not generated)

**`data/voice_test/utterances.jsonl`** — ~150 held-out fictional text utterances (product §13.4), with optional team-recorded audio (E-07) in `data/voice_test/audio/`. Keys: `utterance_id!`, `language!` (`en/hi/mixed`), `script_variant!` (`english/devanagari/romanised_hindi/code_switched`), `text!`, `intent!`, `slots!` (object with expected values), `negated!`, `should_create_record!`, `expected_confirmation!` (`implicit/explicit/none`, technical spec SD-10), `context_state!` (MachineState), `paraphrase_family_id!`, `speaker_group_id?`, `asr_condition!` (`clean/vosk_corrupted/recorded_audio`), `split!` (`test/challenge`), `source!` (`synthetic_text/team_recorded`), `audio_asset_id?`, `review_status!` (`draft/human_reviewed`), `data_origin!`. English, Devanagari Hindi, Romanised Hindi and code-switched slices are reported separately (§12.6). Tamil is not included (technical spec SD-01). No test/challenge text, paraphrase family or recorded speaker group may enter training or validation.

**`data/voice_train/intent_examples.jsonl`** — one reviewed example for the multilingual DistilBERT, separate from the held-out test set. Keys: `example_id!`, `text!`, `intent!`, `language!` (`en/hi/mixed`), `script_variant!`, `paraphrase_family_id!`, `speaker_group_id?`, `asr_condition!`, `context_state!`, `source!` (`synthetic_text/team_recorded`), `review_status!` (`human_reviewed` for trainable rows), `split!` (`train/validation`), `data_origin!`. `content:build` projects trainable rows to `packages/content/voice/intent_examples.<lang>.jsonl` (`text`, `intent`) with `lang = en` for English, `hi` for Devanagari and Romanised Hindi, `mixed` for code-switched; `en` and `hi` need at least 40 examples per launch intent (technical spec §5.4.7). Splits are grouped by paraphrase family and speaker/template; validation selects the confidence and top-two-margin thresholds. Slots and negation remain deterministic and are tested with `voice_test`, not learned.

## 5. Generation and validation contract

The generator creates a small latent event timeline first, then emits truthful observations/reports and deterministic projections. A truck queue may cause an idle, but the **reported reason** can be late, absent or corrected; rule outputs are recomputed from visible inputs. Generate realistic correlations (weather ↔ visibility, material ↔ production, congestion ↔ waits, signal faults ↔ missing data) without making them perfectly deterministic. Include counterexamples so a model cannot simply learn the generator's equation or infer blame from operator identity. Publish every effect and range in `docs/GENERATOR_ASSUMPTIONS.md`; label illustrative safety thresholds as such. Values in technical spec §8.22 are starting assumptions, not measured Cat coefficients.

`manifest.json` contains `schema_version` (`1.2.0`), `generator_version`, `seed`, `anchor_date`, `generated_at` (fixed/reproducible for byte-identical builds), `data_origin`, `profile_versions`, `files` (`path`, `rows`, `sha256`, `grain`), `split_policy`, `assumptions_sha256`, and `limitations`. `--effect-scale 0.5/1.5` gets separate manifests and directories. Sort rows and JSON keys canonically, fix float precision and line endings, and exclude machine-specific wall-clock timestamps from deterministic outputs.

Validation gates (`datagen/validate.py`, run by `pnpm ml:generate` and TC-62) before any model training:

1. Every file parses with exactly the columns/keys of §4; the manifest hashes/counts match; a fixed seed yields identical bytes; a different seed differs.
2. Keys are unique; foreign keys resolve; `fleet.csv` has 100 distinct machines with 24 `detailed` rows matching `machines.csv` and 76 `status_only` rows; 48 operators; about 2,500 tasks, none on wheel loaders; site/class/task/profile/unit combinations are valid; `(machine_id, planned_date, sequence)` is unique.
3. Times respect chronology: forecast issued by estimate time, report no earlier than its event, correction after original, alert clear after raise, incident post-snapshot after trigger, handover acknowledgment after item creation.
4. Task accounting sums to elapsed time within ± 0.1 min; the active target is positive for training rows; no outcome, reason, alert or incident field enters pre-start feature encoding; `baseline_minutes` recomputes from the profile and site job efficiency.
5. Sensor dropouts produce null metrics and `missing_signal_names`, never zero/false; required cool-down, reported wait and unexplained idle produce distinct labels; an acknowledged alert has a later `cleared` transition before it is counted as resolved.
6. Every flat-file row matches its ledger entry (`summary_id`, `alert_event_id`, idle and shift IDs); each started task's original `inference/estimate.context` equals its `*_at_start` columns; incident chain hashes verify.
7. Temporally held-out and unseen-operator evaluations use the declared fixed splits; `split_*` columns never appear in features.
8. Organiser files remain untouched; their rows are mapped separately with no invented lockout or seat-occupancy state.

Voice files are checked by `content:check` and `voice:export-tokens`: train/validation/test/challenge groups are disjoint by text, paraphrase family and speaker/template, and each launch intent meets the per-language minimum.

## 6. Why these fields, and what remains an assumption

| Design choice | Product consequence | Evidence / status |
|---|---|---|
| Quantity, material, machine profile, site job efficiency and dated conditions are separate fields. | Baseline and correction can be explained independently; the app can compare a planner estimate on the same task. | Cat's Performance Handbook gives a job-efficiency table and bucket payload method; its factors are planning examples, **not** the generator's validated coefficients. [Cat Performance Handbook, ed. 50](https://wheelercat.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Cat-Performance-Handbook-Edition-50-June-2022.pdf), [Cat wheel-loader productivity guidance](https://www.cat.com/en_US/articles/for-owners/how-to-calculate-cat-wheel-loader-productivity.html). |
| Work, wait, break and pause are separate from wall-clock elapsed. | A reported site delay changes finish time and attribution without falsely slowing the operator's active rate. | ShiftMate F4/F9; Cat VisionLink also distinguishes working/idle time, cycles, payload and fuel at machine/site level. [VisionLink Productivity](https://www.cat.com/en_US/products/new/technology/visionlink/visionlink/132084.html). |
| Event time, receipt time, forecast issuance and missingness are explicit. | Offline sync, stale-signal safety and historical estimates stay reproducible. | ShiftMate principles 4–5 and F13; ISO/TS 15143-3 defines server-side telematics exchange, **not** on-board CAN collection, so this schema does not pretend to be an ISO CAN format. [ISO/TS 15143-3:2020](https://www.iso.org/standard/76394.html). |
| Proximity episodes live in authored scenarios with relative motion, type, quality and scripted expectations. | Approaching/departing, nuisance alarms and feed outages are testable, rather than accuracy on a distance-only rule. | NIOSH distinguishes true, nuisance, false and missed alarms and emphasizes situational context. Its study does **not** validate ShiftMate's illustrative distances. [NIOSH surface-mining recommendations](https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/docs/mining/UserFiles/works/pdfs/2007-146.pdf). |
| Synthetic provenance is inside each row as well as in the manifest; sensitivity runs are separate. | Demo/evaluation cannot accidentally be presented as field results. | ShiftMate principle 13 and §17.2; NIST recommends evaluating synthetic data against intended use. [NIST synthetic-data guide](https://pages.nist.gov/HLG-MOS_Synthetic_Data_Test_Drive/guide.html). |
| Planned start and sequence per task, Safe Exit transitions as `A-EXIT-UNSEC` alerts, and disjoint bilingual utterance groups are explicit. | Downstream impact can say "unavailable" instead of inventing a risk; Safe Exit history never treats missing data as secured; test phrases never leak into ONNX training. | Product F4-R9–R11, F6-R6–R9, F11-R5–R6 and §17; technical spec §§5.3.2, 8.2, 8.6.9, 8.13 and 8.22. |

**Still assumed, pending generation:** exact effect sizes, distribution shapes, missing-signal rates, condition transition probabilities, report latency, wait frequency, and acceptable challenge coverage. They live in versioned generator config with rationales and sensitivity runs. This schema fixes the *meaning and structure* of data, not a claim that those parameter values are true on a real site.
